content.value_statement: Service mesh traffic rules are hard to design safely across routes, retries, and releases. This skill provides Istio templates and review guidance for production traffic policies.
actual_capabilities: Explains Istio VirtualService, DestinationRule, Gateway, and ServiceEntry roles.
Provides routing templates for header-based routing and weighted canary releases.
Shows resilience patterns for circuit breakers, retries, timeouts, and outlier detection.
Includes traffic mirroring and fault injection examples for testing service behavior.
Lists istioctl commands for analyzing routes, endpoints, and proxy logs.
limitations: Does not apply manifests or change a Kubernetes cluster by itself.
Examples use placeholder service names and must be adapted before deployment.
Does not validate compatibility with every Istio or Kubernetes version.
Does not replace production change review, monitoring, or rollback planning.

use_cases.title: Plan a Canary Release
use_cases.description: Define weighted routing and subset policies for a controlled service rollout.

use_cases.title: Improve Service Resilience
use_cases.description: Add timeouts, retries, connection pools, and outlier detection to reduce cascading failures.

use_cases.title: Review Mesh Routing Changes
use_cases.description: Compare proposed Istio resources against routing, gateway, and load balancing best practices.

prompt_templates.title: Create Basic Routing
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for one service route.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an Istio VirtualService and DestinationRule plan for service <service> in namespace <namespace>. Route default traffic to version <version>.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Canary Rollout
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an Istio canary rollout for <service>. Start with <canary_percent> percent traffic to canary and include validation and rollback checks.

prompt_templates.title: Add Resilience Policies
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this service behavior and propose Istio timeout, retry, connection pool, and outlier detection settings for <service>.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Full Traffic Change
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this Istio traffic management change for routing correctness, blast radius, observability, and rollback readiness: <change_summary>.

output_examples.input: Plan a ten percent canary for the payments service.
output_examples.output: A rollout plan that defines stable and canary subsets, shifts ten percent traffic, verifies metrics, and preserves a rollback path.

output_examples.input: Improve resilience for a service with intermittent upstream failures.
output_examples.output: Recommended timeout, retry, connection pool, and outlier detection settings with notes about failure amplification risks.

output_examples.input: Review an ingress gateway route for an API service.
output_examples.output: A checklist covering host matching, gateway binding, TLS credential use, route prefix behavior, and deployment validation.

best_practices: Start with simple routing rules and add traffic policy complexity incrementally.
Set explicit timeouts, retries, and circuit breaker limits before production rollout.
Validate every change with istioctl analysis, metrics, and a rollback plan.
anti_patterns: Do not mirror production traffic into unsafe or unprepared environments.
Do not overuse retries without limits, because they can amplify failures.
Do not deploy weighted routing without matching DestinationRule subsets.

faq.question: What does this skill help configure?
faq.answer: It helps design Istio routing, load balancing, canary releases, retries, timeouts, circuit breakers, gateways, and traffic mirroring.

faq.question: Does it run commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. It documents example istioctl diagnostics, but users decide when to run commands in their own environment.

faq.question: Can it deploy manifests to my cluster?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and templates, but deployment requires your own Kubernetes tooling and approval process.

faq.question: Which Istio resources are covered?
faq.answer: It covers VirtualService, DestinationRule, Gateway, ServiceEntry concepts, subsets, load balancing, and traffic policies.

faq.question: Is it suitable for production changes?
faq.answer: It can support production planning, but you must adapt examples, test them, monitor results, and maintain rollback steps.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, and Claude Code use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code compatible workflows.
